newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace protests at genetically-altered grain.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace protests at genetically-altered grain.

text.p: Greenpeace staged two separate protests in Europe on Thursday against genetically-altered strains of feed grain.
In Hamburg it disrupted the loading of a maize cargo on to trains bound for the Czech republic, while on the Rhine it blocked a barge loaded with soybeans headed for Switzerland.
They were the latest of several similar Greenpeace blockades in recent weeks.
In Hamburg, activists chained themselves to trains and displayed banners in German and Czech saying "Stop gene maize now."

The leader of Greenpeace in the Czech Republic, Hana Pernicova, who was present during the protest, said her country did not have any laws regulating how genetically manipulated products should be treated.
The EU Commission is due to decide on December 18 whether to allow imports of such modified maize, made by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG.
Until then, it is illegal to market it in the EU, but Greenpeace says cargoes may have reached Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and Portugal.
The Rhine protest was against modified soybeans originating in the United States.
The new type of bean was developed by U.S. chemicals group Monsanto to be resistant to its own new "super weedkiller" Roundup.

Environmental groups describe the Roundup technology as a risky experiment with nature although the Monsanto strain of bean has been given a clean bill of health by U.S. and EU authorities, who say it poses no danger to the human food chain.
